findings: Blocking acceptance violation: [expand.c] creates a rewritten SVG buffer by copying source intervals and inserting generated markup (lines 110–124, 141–159); [clip.c] copies clip children into a generated SVG scratch buffer (lines 155–165). The work order explicitly says “Avoid copying or rewriting source bytes.” Retaining the original bytes in the final document does not satisfy that constraint.

Memory safety: [expand.c] indexes `hidden[d]` in a 65-entry array without bounding `d` (line 177). The XML tokenizer accepts nesting depths up to 256, and this scan runs before the shape decoder’s depth check. An input with an element deeper than 64 can write past the array, including when there is no live `<use>`.

Reference validation gap: [reference.c] skips `<defs>` and `<symbol>` subtrees during `<use>` validation (lines 117–124), while [expand.c] accepts nested `xlink:href` without checking that `xlink` is bound (lines 130–132). A live use that expands a definition containing an unbound `xlink:href="#id"` can therefore bypass the required namespace-binding check.

Evidence and acceptance are inconsistent with this candidate. `executor-report.json` and `fuzz-report.json` identify source revision `dc8b9980b37ded9d16bc0c3d484797c9ce8e7c96`, not candidate `ae14e9032d58b855981451e76ea7fa334a8cc836`; `reference-matrix.json` says use, gradients, and clipping are unimplemented, contrary to the checked-in implementation and comparison cases. Also, `full-checks.txt` records CTest at 11/12 and `./dev asan`, `./dev ubsan`, and `./dev verify` exiting 8, so AC-1 and AC-4 are not met by the recorded evidence.
summary: The candidate has a blocking source-byte contract violation and a depth-triggered out-of-bounds write. Nested xlink references also bypass namespace validation, and the checked-in evidence does not establish acceptance for this commit.
